Hi Bob,

If you look and the CrossTable function definition you will see that it uses 'cat' to format the table and then invisibly returns a list. When you run it through dlply or by without assigning the result to anything you are implicitly printing the resulting list. So you see two sets of output: the cat'ed output produced by CrossTable, and the printed list. This has little to do with either by or dlply, as you will get the same behavior with

tst.dat <- expand.grid(x=c("a", "b"), y=c("C", "D"), g=c("group1", "group2"))

print(my_CrossTable(mydata100))

Presumably you want something like 

tst.dat <- expand.grid(x=c("a", "b"), y=c("C", "D"), g=c("group1", "group2"))

my_CrossTable <- function(x) {
  with(x,{
       cat("Cross classification for ", unique(as.character(g)), ":\n", sep="")
       CrossTable(x, y,
                  chisq = TRUE, format = "SAS")})}


library(plyr)
d_ply(tst.dat, "g", my_CrossTable)

Best,
Ista

On Fri, Dec 28, 2012 at 10:30 AM, Bob <muen...@tennessee.edu> wrote:
Hi All,
 
I've been using gmodels CrossTable function for years since it makes SAS & SPSS users happy with its familiar output. Recently I used ddply on it by gender and got odd output. The crosstabulations are not labled by gender and additional tables appear with row proportion, column proportion, etc. which ARE labeled by gender. I doubt this is a ddply bug since by() gives exactly the same results. Does anyone know why the output is so different from the regular output?
 
Thanks,
Bob

On Monday, December 31, 2012 4:11:30 PM UTC-5, izahn wrote:
Hi Bob,

If you look and the CrossTable function definition you will see that it uses 'cat' to format the table and then invisibly returns a list. When you run it through dlply or by without assigning the result to anything you are implicitly printing the resulting list. So you see two sets of output: the cat'ed output produced by CrossTable, and the printed list. This has little to do with either by or dlply, as you will get the same behavior with

tst.dat <- expand.grid(x=c("a", "b"), y=c("C", "D"), g=c("group1", "group2"))

print(my_CrossTable(mydata100))

Presumably you want something like 

tst.dat <- expand.grid(x=c("a", "b"), y=c("C", "D"), g=c("group1", "group2"))

my_CrossTable <- function(x) {
  with(x,{
       cat("Cross classification for ", unique(as.character(g)), ":\n", sep="")
       CrossTable(x, y,
                  chisq = TRUE, format = "SAS")})}


library(plyr)
d_ply(tst.dat, "g", my_CrossTable)

Best,
Ista
